## Code's readings to build (each is Code's; each goes into a new PIN text, declared at LOCK v1.0, strikable until v1.0's commit)

### (a) the posting bar and the rewrite comparison (PIN-44)
- **Scope.** The bar is "the pass bar for the posting's re-run on the posted text" (C7), so it is rendered on a run whose
  table kind is `posted`. On an `of-record` run the output records the bar as not applicable (with that reason), and no
  rewrite list is taken.
- **The rewrite list**: a new declared input, CLI `posting --rewrites PATH`, REQUIRED on a `posted` run and REFUSED
  (exit 2) on an `of-record` run. Schema `{"schema": "m-posting-rewrites-v1", "posting": "v1", "rows": [row_id, ...]}`,
  exact key set; `rows` a list of distinct non-empty strings (may be empty). It must be committed at HEAD with identical
  working-tree bytes, through the same `env.committed` rule the sentence table uses. It is read only after
  `analyzer_binding` (PIN-42's "before any input is read"). Its path and sha256 are recorded in the output's `inputs`
  (`_file_rec`).
- **The bar**: PASS iff (i) the enumeration of this run is empty AND (ii) the dose note is present iff the flag
  (compute (ii) explicitly from `dose_note(...)`'s status against the flag of record, not only through clause (c)).
  The output's `bar` block: `{"applies": true, "verdict": "PASS"|"FAIL", "enumeration_empty": bool,
  "dose_note_iff_flag": bool, "residue": [row_id, ...] (this run's enumerated rows, in table order), "comparison": {...}}`.
- **The comparison** ("compares the posting re-run's enumeration with the VERDICTS enumeration with the PI's rewrites
  applied ... reporting any row that differs"):
  - The comparator ("the VERDICTS enumeration"): Q-F0's VERDICTS output `verdicts_dir/Q-F0_VERDICTS.json`, its
    `v1_outputs`' enumeration (check how `verdicts` writes it; use the stored rows). Where that file does not exist (a
    Q-F0 Clock NOT-RUN path, where the table is built at the posting: m:278, PIN-40), the comparator is the posting's
    own of-record output `out/POSTING-v1_outputs.of-record.json`'s enumeration. Where neither exists, the posted run is
    refused (exit 2): there is nothing to compare with. Record which comparator was used (`"comparator": {"kind":
    "verdicts"|"posting-of-record", "path": ..., "sha256": ...}`).
  - Expected = the comparator's rows with any row whose `row_id` is in the rewrite list removed. Actual = this run's
    enumeration. Report: `only_actual` (row ids enumerated now but not expected), `only_expected` (expected but not
    enumerated now), `changed` (in both, with a differing `clauses` value), and `rewrites_not_in_comparator` (rewrite ids
    the comparator never enumerated: informational). `differs` = any of the first three non-empty.
  - The comparison is reported; it does not decide PASS/FAIL (R2: "reporting any row that differs").
- **FAIL**: a FAIL writes nothing (so that the re-run after further rewriting can write once), prints the residue by row
  id and the comparison, and exits 5. Extend PIN-26's text with the posting's 5 (FAIL against C7's bar, PIN-44; nothing
  written) and make main()'s exit mapping carry it; 0/2/4 unchanged. A PASS writes as now (write-once, identical on
  re-run) and exits 0.
- The output document gains `bar` (and, on posted runs, `inputs.rewrites` and the comparator record). `outputs` (from
  `v1_outputs`) is untouched. If a key-set assertion covers the posting output document, extend it.

### (b) a fired end look without a matching pause (PIN-45)
A VERDICTS refusal at V2, placed right after the existing PIN-10 STOP/no-end-look refusal and BEFORE PIN-9's branch
(otherwise a deleted pause reads as "no pause" and is accepted). Exit 2 (AnlRefusal). It mirrors the writer's
invariants in `valence_core/m/stages.py` (read `_campaign_end` ~2215-2270, `_stop_end_look` ~2273-2326, `campaign_look`
~1955-1990, the cadence-look pause ~2120-2135; do not import private stages helpers):
- An end look is **fired** iff `end_look["fired"]` is true OR any of its `results` has `fired` true (a hand edit that
  clears `fired` but leaves a fired result is still a fired end look).
- A fired end look **without** `end_is_look` (a fresh evaluation, terminal or STOP): `pauses[-1]` must be
  `{"kind": "end_look", "look": "end", "at_launches": end_look["at_launches"], "bars": [names of fired results, in
  order]}` (its adjudication may be anything).
- A fired end look **with** `end_is_look` k (a cadence look reused at a multiple of 40): SOME pause in `pauses` must be
  `{"kind": "look", "look": k, "at_launches": end_look["at_launches"], "bars": [...same...]}` — not necessarily the last
  (at a terminal reuse the cadence pause was raised and adjudicated before the end, and a `schedule_exhausted` pause may
  follow it at the same n).
- Otherwise refuse: "REFUSED: a fired end look records no matching pause (...) -- not written by the lock's package".
- An unfired end look needs no pause; this edit adds no check for that direction.

### (c) the end look's launch count (PIN-46)
A VERDICTS refusal at V2 beside (b), before PIN-9: where `campaign.end_look` is recorded, its `at_launches` must equal
`len(ck["sessions"])` (the launches recorded; a G-VER record is quarantined in the stop block, never a session). Never
use provenance `launched` sums. Applies at every end that records an end look (STOP and terminal alike) — Code's
reading; Code's round-2 block scoped it to the STOP. Refuse: "REFUSED: the end look's launch count (...) is not the
launches recorded (...) -- not written by the lock's package". Order (b) and (c) so that the battery shows each one's
own message on its own case.

## The battery (PIN-24's rules: a skip is a failure; EXPECTED_CHECKS and REQUIRED_COVERAGE updated)

Reader-path cases are hand edits of production-written stub campaigns (see `_Camp`, `no_end_look`, C3-* cases, ~:4264-
5100). Each refusal case must show: the refusal's own message, exit/refusal at V2, ZERO `release_full` calls, nothing
written; and its unedited control keeps its current result.
- (b): drop the matching pause from (1) the terminal COMPLETE fired case (`ck_el`), (2) the hair STOP fresh at 6
  (`ck_hf`), (3) the G-VER STOP case that records a fresh fired end look if one exists (`ck_ge`; check), (4) the hair STOP
  at 40 reused (`ck_hl`, pause kind `look`); (5) alter the pause's kind; (6) alter its `at_launches`; (7) alter its
  `bars`; (8) clear `end_look.fired` while a result stays fired, with the pause dropped; (9) refusal order: a dropped pause
  together with a supplied `--adjudication` is refused by (b), not accepted; (10) positive control: a terminal reuse
  (end_is_look) whose matching cadence pause is NOT the last pause is accepted (build one with the production writers if
  none exists; otherwise a hand-built copy that keeps every invariant).
- (c): (1) the end look reused at 40 against 41 sessions recorded (the D2 review's mutant scenario,
  results/raw/2026-10-10_m-d2-c9-build_review.txt ~868-872; there the STOP was at launch 42 after a silent look 1 at 40 —
  read it and build the closest case), (2) `ck_el` with `at_launches` +1 and -1, (3) a STOP case with -1.
- (a): PASS on a synthetic posted table that fires nothing (the placeholder always fires; build a minimal posted table
  under the battery's temp-repo fixtures), with a rewrite list and a comparator; FAIL with residue (exit 5, nothing
  written, the residue printed); the dose conjunct false under each flag value; the comparison matching (differs false)
  and differing (each of only_actual / only_expected / changed); comparator selection (VERDICTS present → verdicts;
  absent with an of-record output → posting-of-record; neither → refused); rewrite-list refusals (missing on posted;
  given on of-record; uncommitted; bad schema; duplicate ids; non-string id); the of-record run's bar "not applicable".
  Rewrite CMD-POSTING-BOTH-KINDS (~:5503-5519) as the new semantics require (its posted copy of a table that enumerates
  rows now FAILs and writes nothing).
- Every new check has a coverage id added to REQUIRED_COVERAGE; EXPECTED_CHECKS = the new total.

## How to test

`SCRATCH/runst15.sh <src.py> <run-id>` clones HEAD into scratch, copies your file over scripts/m_analyze.py and runs the
battery (11 s at HEAD; 384/384). Output: `SCRATCH/out/<run-id>.txt`. Iterate until `N/N m_analyze battery checks
pass` and EXIT 0. Use run-ids prefixed `b1_`. Also run the m_sessions self-test once in a clone with your analyzer
copied in (adapt the runner's last command to `scripts/m_sessions.py --selftest`, in your own script under
SCRATCH/build/) and confirm its count passes (796/796 at HEAD), to show the driver's self-test is unaffected.

## Return

A build report (markdown): every change with its line numbers in `m_analyze.r1.py`; the unified diff stat; the new PIN
texts verbatim (PIN-44, -45, -46 and PIN-26 as extended) and every site comment; every reading you made beyond this spec
(each labelled Code's); the battery's new check count and coverage ids; the final battery and m_sessions self-test summary
lines; the sha256 of `m_analyze.r1.py`; and anything in this spec you found wrong against the code or the record (do not
silently depart from it — report).

**PIN-44:** "Declared at LOCK v1.0, built at step 15 on the seat's round-2 item 3 (a) (lock §9.6): \"the `posting` command renders PASS/FAIL against the bar (PASS iff the enumeration under (a), (b) and (c) is empty and the dose note is present iff the flag); and it compares the posting re-run's enumeration with the VERDICTS enumeration with the PI's rewrites applied (a declared input: the rewrite list, by row id), reporting any row that differs.\" The bar reads the posted table's declared classification (the seat: \"no analyzer reads prose\"). Code's readings: C7's bar is \"The pass bar for the posting's re-run on the posted text\", so it is rendered on a run whose table kind is posted; an of-record run records it as not applicable, with that reason, and takes no rewrite list. The rewrite list is a declared input, posting --rewrites PATH: {schema m-posting-rewrites-v1, posting v1, rows: [row_id, ...]}, exact key set, rows distinct non-empty strings (may be empty); required on a posted run and refused on an of-record run (exit 2); committed at HEAD with identical working-tree bytes (the sentence table's rule) and read only after PIN-42's binding; its path and sha256 recorded in inputs.rewrites. PASS iff (i) this run's enumeration is empty and (ii) the dose note is present iff the flag of record, (ii) computed from dose_note's own status (present iff dose_note(True, table) is 'carried': the table carries a dose-note span), not only through clause (c). The comparator ('the VERDICTS enumeration') is Q-F0's VERDICTS output in the verdicts directory, its stored v1_outputs enumeration; where that file does not exist (Q-F0 NOT-RUN: on its Clock path the table of record is built at the posting, m:278, PIN-40; a no-first-read NOT-RUN from `verdicts` records no enumeration either), the posting's own of-record output in the out directory, its outputs' enumeration; neither, or a comparator recording no enumeration, is refused (exit 2); its kind, path and sha256 are recorded. Expected = the comparator's rows less those the rewrite list names; actual = this run's enumeration; reported: only_actual, only_expected, changed (in both, with differing clauses), rewrites_not_in_comparator (informational) and differs (any of the first three). The comparison is reported; it does not decide PASS / FAIL. A PASS writes once (identical on a re-run; exit 0); a FAIL writes nothing, prints the residue by row id and the comparison, and exits 5 (PIN-26). The output gains `bar` {applies, verdict, enumeration_empty, dose_note_iff_flag, residue, comparison}; `outputs` is unchanged."

**PIN-45:** "Declared at LOCK v1.0, built at step 15 on the seat's round-2 item 3 (lock §9.6), which orders \"(b) a fired end look without a matching pause\" built \"as VERDICTS refusals\" that \"guard the checkpoint against a hand edit\". Code's reading, mirroring the writer's invariants in stages (_campaign_end, _stop_end_look, run_campaign's cadence-look pause): an end look is fired iff its `fired` is true or any of its results is fired (a hand edit clearing `fired` beside a fired result is still a fired end look); its bars are the names of its fired results, in order. A fired end look evaluated fresh (no end_is_look; terminal or STOP) is matched only by the campaign's last pause being {kind end_look, look 'end', at_launches the end look's, bars its fired bars}; one reusing cadence look k (end_is_look k, at a multiple of 40) by some pause {kind look, look k, at_launches the end look's, bars} -- not necessarily the last (at a terminal reuse the cadence pause was raised and adjudicated before the end, and a schedule_exhausted pause may follow it at the same n). A pause's adjudication may be anything (PIN-9 rules on it). Otherwise a structural refusal at V2 (exit 2; nothing released or written), after PIN-46's and before PIN-9's branch, so that a deleted pause is never read as no pause. An unfired end look needs no pause; none is checked."

**PIN-46:** "Declared at LOCK v1.0, built at step 15 on the seat's round-2 item 3 (lock §9.6), which orders \"(c) the end look's launch count\" built \"as VERDICTS refusals\" that \"guard the checkpoint against a hand edit\". Code's reading: wherever campaign.end_look is recorded, at every end that records one (STOP and terminal alike; Code's round-2 block had scoped it to the STOP), its at_launches is an int equal to len(sessions), the launches recorded (a G-VER record is quarantined in the stop block, never a session); provenance `launched` sums are never used. Otherwise a structural refusal at V2 (exit 2; nothing released or written), after PIN-10's and before PIN-45's, so that each refusal shows its own message on its own case."

I checked every seat quote against LOCK-m-F0.md §9.5-9.6 (lines 1648-1656). They are exact apart from the markdown bold and italics, which I dropped. C7's phrase keeps its capital T.

## 4. Readings beyond the spec (all Code's)

1. **Check order.** The order is PIN-10, then (c), then (b), then PIN-9. (c) has to come before (b): otherwise the case of a fired end look with `at_launches` ±1 would show (b)'s message, because its pause's count no longer matches.
2. **What (c) counts as "recorded".** An end look is recorded when `campaign.end_look is not None`. A non-object end look counts as recorded with no launch count, and is refused. `at_launches` must have type int, so 4.0 is refused.
3. **How (b) matches a pause.**
   - `kind`, `look` and `at_launches` must be equal and of the same type; `bars` must be the same list.
   - "Fired" is read by truthiness, as stages does.
   - A reuse is detected as `"end_is_look" in end_look`, as `stages._report` does.
   - A `results` value that is not a list is treated as having no results.
4. **The bar's (ii).** It is computed as `(dose_note(True, table)["status"] == "carried") == flag`. `dose_note(False, …)` always reports "none (struck)", so it cannot show whether the table carries a dose note.
5. **The comparator.**
   - `verdicts-dir/Q-F0_VERDICTS.json` is used when it exists, even beside an of-record output.
   - Otherwise `out/POSTING-v1_outputs.of-record.json` is used.
   - If neither exists, the run is refused.
   - A comparator that cannot be parsed, or that lacks an enumeration of items with a str `row_id` and a list `clauses`, is refused (exit 2).
   - Its record goes in `bar.comparison.comparator`; the spec did not say where.
6. **The shape of the comparison.**
   - `changed` is a list of `{row_id, expected, actual}`, holding clause lists.
   - Each list keeps its source's order.
   - `rewrites_not_in_comparator` never sets `differs`.
7. **Output and parsing.**
   - FAIL lines are printed on stdout; refusals stay on stderr.
   - A PASS appends the same three bar lines.
   - The rewrite list is parsed from the committed bytes, so the recorded sha256 is the sha256 of exactly what was parsed.
8. **Read order inside `run_posting`.** The rewrite list and the comparator are read after the tuple, the cross-check, the table and the PIN-40 loop, because the table's kind decides which rewrite-list rule applies. Everything is read after PIN-42's binding.
9. **Of-record outputs.** They also gain `bar`, set to `{"applies": false, "reason": ...}`.
10. **Battery cases I added beyond the spec's list:**
    - **C3-ENDLOOK-PAUSE-NOT-LAST:** a fresh end look whose pause is followed by a hand-appended, adjudicated pause. It is refused.
    - **Float launch count:** `at_launches` set to 4.0, inside C3-ENDLOOK-COUNT-STOP.
    - **Direct `posting_bar` call:** with an empty enumeration, inside CMD-POSTING-BAR-DOSE.
    - **Commit double:** one that reports a problem beside bytes, inside CMD-POSTING-REWRITES-FORM.
    - **CMD-POSTING-EXIT-5:** goes through `main()` with `production_env` patched.
    - **CMD-POSTING-REWRITES-AFTER-BINDING:** the PIN-42 order for the rewrite list.
11. **How (b)(10)'s positive control is built.** The production writers build it in three `run_campaign` invocations. In the battery only, `stages.load_committed` is patched to cut the committed A0s schedule to its first 20 cells. That is the only way a `schedule_exhausted` pause can follow the cadence pause at n=40: the real schedule has 960 cells, and stages enforces floor ≤ launch count ≤ n_sched. The run goes as follows:
    - Look 1 fires at 40 (PAUSE), and the seat resumes it.
    - A0s exhausts its schedule at 40 (PAUSE), with 19 of 20 domain and floor 20.
    - The PI stops it (PI-STOP at 40), with look 1 reused and fired.

    The identity records n=20 for A0s. I confirmed the sequence first in `SCRATCH/build/exp/exp_reuse40.py`.

## 6. Where the spec is wrong or open against the code or the record

1. **The comparator fallback.** The spec gives the fallback's case as "a Q-F0 Clock NOT-RUN path". A no-first-read NOT-RUN written by `verdicts` also has no VERDICTS file, and its output records no enumeration. The file-existence rule handles both the same way, and PIN-44 says so.
2. **No key-set assertion to extend.** No key-set assertion covers the posting output document (CMD-POSTING-KEYSET covers the tuple's reasons and pending), so I extended nothing. The new PASS check asserts the bar block's key set.
3. **CMD-POSTING-TABLE-BOUND also broke.** The spec names only BOTH-KINDS, but TABLE-BOUND broke the same way: its posted run had no rewrite list, and its `bd` VERDICTS stub had no `v1_outputs`. My minimal fix:
   - the stub gains an empty enumeration;
   - the posted run uses the minimal table with an empty rewrite list.

   It PASSes and is written, so `sbo == spo == "written"` still holds. The check's text is unchanged.
4. **The D2 review's own scenario is not reproduced.** I built (c)(1) on `res_lp` (the G-VER STOP at 42, with 41 sessions recorded), as the spec directs. The D2 review's own scenario is a hair STOP at 42 with 42 recorded; the battery has no such campaign. The hand edit applies the review's mutant `endislook_any_look`.
5. **PIN-7 and PIN-10 do not name the new refusals.** Their texts list VERDICTS' V2 structural refusals but not PIN-45 or PIN-46. I did not edit them, per scope; the seat may want to.
6. **No direct 796/796 for m_sessions.** The m_sessions self-test needs the analyzer committed at HEAD. A direct 796/796 with the new analyzer would need a commit inside the scratch clone, which is a git write, so I did not make it. The controls in §7 stand in for it.
7. **Equivalent forms.** Two pieces of the new code cannot change a result on their own.
   - The bar's (ii) conjunct can never decide a `run_posting` outcome by itself: clause (c) is two-sided and `table_problems` requires an f1-corr-line row, so an empty enumeration already implies (ii). Only the direct `posting_bar` call exercises it.
   - Under `stages._committed`, `rwp or rwb is None` is the same as `rwb is None`, because problems always come with bytes of None. The sentence table's check has the same form.
8. **The texts don't say strikable.** PIN-44, -45 and -46 say "Declared at LOCK v1.0", per the marker rule. They are strikable until v1.0's commit, but the texts do not say so.

---- CODE'S DISPOSITIONS OF ROUND 1 (disp_r1.md), verbatim
# Round 1: Code's dispositions (for the fixer; the review JSON is SCRATCH/r1_reviews.json)

Every CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE finding is applied, as below. Several REFUTED ones are applied too, where the change costs
nothing. Each change from spec_r1 is a reading of Code's: say so in the PIN text, and list it in the fix report.

## (b) and (c): the writer's invariants (stages.py; the refusals lens F1 to F4, the battery lens ADQ-1 to ADQ-6 and ADQ-9, the fidelity lens FA-3 and FA-4)
- **F1, F2 (adopted).** This replaces spec_r1's "(its adjudication may be anything)":
  - A pause **raised at the end** must be `pauses[-1]` and must carry adjudication None (an ended campaign is never
    resumed; stages.py:2129 is the only writer of an adjudication; resume.apply_end appends the end pause with None).
    End-raised pauses are: a fresh end look, terminal or STOP; and a reused look at a hair-trigger STOP on a multiple of
    40 (kind look).
  - A **cadence look's pause reused** at a terminal or G-VER end must exist somewhere in `pauses`, matching, with a str
    adjudication (ruled through stages before the end).
  - Use the refusals lens's validated replacement (its probe_bc_9.py) as the base.
  - Rebuild REF-SURPLUS-ADJ-ADJUDICATED (~:5539-5542) on a production-written checkpoint whose last pause stages ruled,
    as F1's fix says. The old fixture's comment is wrong for an end pause.
- **F3 (adopted, but kept inside (b) and (c), with no new refusal class).** For an end look carrying `end_is_look` k:
  - (b): the end look is **fired** iff any of the following holds: its own `fired`; any of its results fired; the
    reused look k as recorded in `ck["looks"]` fired (its `result.fired`, or any of its results fired). Code's reading:
    "a fired end look" read through the look it reuses.
  - (c): the end look's launch count must also be the reused look's. `ck["looks"]` must record a look k whose
    `at_launches` equals `end_look["at_launches"]` (and that already equals len(sessions)), else (c)'s refusal.
  - Do NOT add the whole-object identity refusal. State the residual limits in PIN-45's text: clearing the flags on the
    reused look as well, or on a fresh end look (F7), cannot be told at V2 without recomputing campaign_look from the
    records, which are pick-bearing until V3.
  - With this in place, h13 (end_is_look edited alone) is refused by (c), because no look 2 is recorded at that n.
    Assert whichever message the build gives, and say which in the case's name.
- **F4 / ADQ-1 to ADQ-6, ADQ-9, FA-3, FA-4.** Add the reviewers' cases h1 to h14 (the refusals lens's
  bc/probe_block2.py.txt and probe_bc_7.py / probe_bc_9.py) and its positive controls P2, P3, P4 (and any others it
  validated), plus the battery lens's:
  - an end look with `fired` true and NO fired result, its pause dropped (the first disjunct alone);
  - a missing `at_launches` key (refused by (c));
  - a two-bar case for bar order (ck_ge fires two);
  - a float at_launches on the pause (type identity, which PIN-45's text must now declare as Code's reading: "compared
    by value and exact type, as the writer writes ints and strs");
  - end_is_look edited alone;
  - bool as a launch count (cap0's one-session checkpoint).
  Each case asserts its refusal's own message, 0 release_full calls and nothing written. Each has a coverage id, and
  EXPECTED_CHECKS is updated.
- **F5, F6** (refuted: no false refusal; correct placement). After the fixes, re-verify that every production-written
  end path is accepted: list them in the report with their run.

## (a): the posting bar (the posting lens A-1 to A-7; FA-5, FA-6, FA-10, FA-11)

## 3. Readings beyond spec_r1 and the dispositions (all Code's)

**Places where spec_r1 is superseded by the dispositions**
- PIN-45's "(its adjudication may be anything)" is replaced by the writer invariant (F1, F2).
- `changed` compares whole items, not just `clauses`.
- A FAIL prints its full record, not just "the residue by row id and the comparison".
- STR-PIN-COMMENTS is exact per lock version, instead of the widened regex.

**Readings of mine (the fixer's)**
1. **PIN-46's reuse refusal.** It keeps PIN-46's prefix but has its own tail: "is not that of the look it reuses (look k, recorded at [...])". Look k is identified by `result.look`, compared by value and exact type; the look's `at_launches` must be an int equal to the end look's.
2. **(b) reading the reused look.** It reads the look that (c) found (`reused_lk`). The bars still come from the end look's own results. So a reused end look whose results were cleared but whose look k is fired is expected to have bars `[]`.
3. **Which end pauses must be last and unadjudicated.** `end_raised = not reused or (STOP and the stop bar not in GVER_BARS)`. The stop record is read defensively: a stop that is not an object counts as "not G-VER", so its pause is treated as end-raised.
4. **Comparator items.** They must carry exactly enumeration()'s fields (`ENUM_ITEM_KEYS`). This goes further than A-5, which asked only for a list `clauses`. The point is that whole-item comparison and FAIL printing then only ever see enumeration fields.
5. **Normalization.** Actual items are put through a JSON round trip before comparing, so in-memory and stored items compare equal.
6. **`same_tuple`** sits at `bar.comparison.same_tuple`. `comparator.tuple` is the comparator's stored tuple, or None if it is missing or not an object.
7. **FAIL line formats** (sorted-key JSON):
   - `POSTING v1: residue i of n, ID: {item}`
   - `POSTING v1: comparison only_actual|only_expected ID: {item}`
   - `POSTING v1: comparison changed ID: expected {…}; actual {…}`
   - `POSTING v1: comparison rewrites not in the comparator: [...]`
   - `POSTING v1: the unwritten record: inputs {…}; comparator {…}; flag {…}; binding {…}`

   A PASS still prints only the three summary lines. The summary's `changed` now lists row ids only.
8. **An empty `--rewrites`.** `Path('')` becomes `'.'`, which is a directory, so it is refused as unreadable. This check comes after the binding and before `env.committed`. An absent path that is not a directory still refuses as "not committed at HEAD".
9. **STR-PIN-COMMENTS details.**
   - The marker regex catches any `# PIN (Code, declared at LOCK X)`, with or without a PIN id.
   - The set of v1.0 entries is taken from register texts that begin "Declared at LOCK v1.0", and must be PIN-44 onward.
   - Planted controls are built by string concatenation, so none of them is itself a marker in the file.
   - Plants beyond the disposition's three (v0.2, new id under v0.1, old id under v1.0): v2.0 and v1.1 (kept from r1), a marker naming no id, and a new register id declared at v0.1.
   - r1's redundant `sites`/`missing`/`extra` are removed (they would have been an equivalent mutant).
10. **New check STR-PIN-V10-TEXTS** (no disposition orders it; it can be struck).
    - It checks that PIN-44/45/46 and their site comments say "Code's reading", never credit the seat, and quote the seat as the battery's own copy has it (R2 3(a), the C7 phrase, the (b)/(c) words).
    - Four planted controls. It kills the text-class survivors p_fa_4 and p_fa_5.
    - p_fa_8 is killed by a new conjunct in EXIT-5 (PIN-26 carries "posting also 5" and "FAIL against C7's bar"). p_fa_9 is killed by FA-6's optional exact-quote conjunct in BAR-NA.
11. **P1-P10 all go into the battery.** P9 runs under a `load_committed` patch that cuts A0s to 2 cells. P10 runs under a patched `resume.hour_cap_exceeded` that binds at 5 launches (the refuter's deterministic form). Both are named in their labels. Each P check asserts its exact fixture description; P6-P10 also assert that PIN-9 asks for the adjudication without it.
12. **How the h-cases are grouped.**
    - h1, h2, h4 in one check; h3 and h14 in one; h9 and h10 in one.
    - h7 plus FA-3's reuse conjunct get their own id (C3-ENDLOOK-PAUSE-LOOK), not folded into PAUSE-KIND.
    - h8 plus the pause's look as 1.0 form C3-ENDLOOK-PAUSE-TYPE.

## Texts

## (b) and (c)
- **R2BC-1 (confirmed).** F1/F2's rule is chosen by the end's class as recorded, so a hand edit to the stop block

  Use ids only; no pick-bearing field is read. If the checkpoint's other V2 checks already pin the class (ended_status,

  still accepted.

  fired only.

## (a)

  is informational). Amend PIN-44.

A pause raised at the end (a fresh end look's; a reused look k's at a hair-trigger STOP, which pre-empted the cadence pause) is matched only by the LAST pause {kind end_look, look 'end' | kind look, look k, at_launches, bars}, unadjudicated (its ruling enters as PIN-9's declared file); a reused look k's at a terminal or G-VER end by SOME pause {kind look, look k, at_launches, bars} carrying a str adjudication (ruled before the end, through stages: by the seat's adjudication, or by the PI's stop text recorded as the pause's ruling (stages.py:2124-2129); a schedule_exhausted pause may follow it at the same n). kind, look and at_launches compare by value and exact type, as the writer writes ints and strs. The rule is chosen by the end's class as recorded, and at a STOP that class is checked by ids against the writer's own assertions (stages._stop_end_look): a hair-trigger STOP's (template, s) is the last session recorded, a G-VER STOP's none of them. const halves = [['the FIRST half of the diff: every hunk whose r5 line number is below 3100 (code, register texts, constants)', 'A'], ['the SECOND half: every hunk at r5 line 3100 or above (the battery: labels, comments, plants)', 'B']]
const sw = await parallel(halves.map(([h, p]) => () => agent(`${COMMON}\nTASK: sweep ${h}. List EVERY added/changed line that cites the seat, a ruling, the PI, m:N or a stages/resume line, one item each (id ${p}01, ${p}02, ...), with the verdict and evidence (the source's exact words). Include OK items too, so the sweep is an inventory.`, { label: `sweep-${p}`, phase: 'Sweep', schema: SCH })))
const all = sw.filter(Boolean).flatMap(x => x.items || [])
const flagged = all.filter(i => i.verdict !== 'OK')
log(`${all.length} citations swept, ${flagged.length} flagged`)
phase('Refute')
let ref = null
if (flagged.length) {
  ref = await agent(`${COMMON}\nSTRICT REFUTER. For each flagged citation below, re-check against the source and try to show the text is right. CONFIRMED = it must change (minimal exact fix); REFUTED = right as written; PLAUSIBLE = unsettled.\nFLAGGED:\n${JSON.stringify(flagged, null, 1)}`, { label: 'refute', phase: 'Refute', schema: { type: 'object', properties: { verdicts: { type: 'array', items: { type: 'object', properties: { id: { type: 'string' }, verdict: { type: 'string', enum: ['CONFIRMED', 'REFUTED', 'PLAUSIBLE'] }, evidence: { type: 'string' }, fix: { type: 'string' } }, required: ['id', 'verdict', 'evidence', 'fix'] } } }, required: ['verdicts'] } })
}
return { swept: all, refute: ref }

---- THE MUTATOR (mut15.py) AND THE RUNNERS (runst15.sh, batch15.sh), verbatim
"""Step-15 mutator: apply ONE mutant to a file in place.
usage: python -I mut15.py <file> <mutant-id>   (mutants from $MUTANTS, default mutants.json beside this script)
A mutant is {"id": ..., "old": ..., "new": ..., "count": 1}: `old` must occur exactly `count` times (default 1);
every occurrence is replaced by `new`. Prints MUTATED <id> or exits 3 with the reason."""
import json, os, sys
f, mid = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
mp = os.environ.get("MUTANTS") or os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)), "mutants.json")
ms = {m["id"]: m for m in json.load(open(mp, encoding="utf-8"))}
if mid not in ms:
    print(f"NO SUCH MUTANT {mid}"); sys.exit(3)
m = ms[mid]
src = open(f, encoding="utf-8").read()
edits = m["edits"] if "edits" in m else [[m["old"], m["new"]]]   # a multi-edit mutant applies every edit
out = src
for o_, n_ in edits:
    want = int(m.get("count", 1)) if "edits" not in m else 1
    got = out.count(o_)
    if got != want:
        print(f"MUTANT {mid}: old occurs {got} times, want {want}"); sys.exit(3)
    out = out.replace(o_, n_)
if out == src:
    print(f"MUTANT {mid}: no change"); sys.exit(3)
open(f, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(out)
print(f"MUTATED {mid}")

#!/bin/zsh
# step 15 analyzer battery / mutation runner (after G-F0m-Qwen's close, 5af9e07). usage:
#   runst15.sh <src.py> <run-id> [mutator.py mutation-id]
# Clones the repository at HEAD (git clone --shared, scratch only), copies <src.py> over scripts/m_analyze.py, applies at
# most ONE mutation, and runs the analyzer battery (m_analyze.py --selftest) under the step-12 net (model imports and
# sockets blocked). Output: <outdir>/<id>.txt (+ .diff). Nothing is committed in the clone.
set -u
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jasondwyer-Documents-code-jspace-lab/adb70afc-5886-490b-a675-abb30f8c425f/scratchpad/step15
R=/Users/jasondwyer/Documents/code/jspace-lab
PY=$R/jlens-qwen36/.venv/bin/python
NET=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jasondwyer-Documents-code-jspace-lab/adb70afc-5886-490b-a675-abb30f8c425f/scratchpad/step12/mt3/net
src=$1; k=$2
mut=${3:-}; mid=${4:-}
O=${OUTDIR:-$S/out}; W=${WDIR:-$S/w}; mkdir -p $O $W
n=$k
cd $W || exit 9
rm -rf $W/$n
git clone -q --shared $R $n || exit 9
cd $W/$n || exit 9
ln -s $R/jlens-qwen36 jlens-qwen36
rm -f $W/$n/data/m/ckpt/*.json
cp $src scripts/m_analyze.py
echo "SOURCE $(shasum -a 256 $src | cut -c1-16) HEAD $(git rev-parse --short HEAD) run $k mutation ${mid:--} (the clone's data/m/ckpt/*.json removed unread)" > $O/$n.txt
if [[ -n $mut ]]; then
  $PY -I $mut scripts/m_analyze.py $mid >> $O/$n.txt 2>&1 || { echo "MUTATE FAILED" >> $O/$n.txt; exit 8; }
fi
diff -u $src scripts/m_analyze.py > $O/$n.diff
SECONDS=0
PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 PYTHONPATH=$NET $PY scripts/m_analyze.py --selftest >> $O/$n.txt 2>&1
echo "EXIT $?" >> $O/$n.txt
echo "SECONDS $SECONDS" >> $O/$n.txt
cd $W && rm -rf $W/$n

#!/bin/zsh
# Code's final mutation batch for step 15's analyzer round. usage: batch15.sh <src.py> <mutants.json> <batch-name>
# Runs the battery once unmutated (baseline) and once per mutant (mut15.py, exact old occurring `count` times), 6 at a time.
set -u
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-jasondwyer-Documents-code-jspace-lab/adb70afc-5886-490b-a675-abb30f8c425f/scratchpad/step15
PY=/Users/jasondwyer/Documents/code/jspace-lab/jlens-qwen36/.venv/bin/python
src=$1; mj=$2; b=$3
export OUTDIR=$S/$b WDIR=$S/w_$b MUTANTS=$mj
mkdir -p $OUTDIR $WDIR
$S/runst15.sh $src 00_baseline
$PY -I -c "import json,sys; [print(m['id']) for m in json.load(open(sys.argv[1]))]" $mj > $OUTDIR/jobs.txt
cat $OUTDIR/jobs.txt | xargs -P 6 -I{} $S/runst15.sh $src {} $S/mut15.py {}
echo BATCH_DONE $(wc -l < $OUTDIR/jobs.txt)
